Experiment_1_Policy_Comparison.setup: 12 diverse tasks evaluated under Latency-First vs Capacity-Aware policies.
Experiment_1_Policy_Comparison.expected: Latency-First achieves lower average latency by aggressively placing sensitive tasks on Edge; Capacity-Aware distributes load more evenly across Fog and Cloud.
Experiment_1_Policy_Comparison.actual: Latency-First avg latency: 80.0 ms vs Capacity-Aware: 91.67 ms. Load balanced across nodes.

Experiment_2_Overload_Scenario.setup: 19 tasks submitted, requesting 130+ CPU cores against a cluster capacity of 84 cores.
Experiment_2_Overload_Scenario.expected: Edge and Fog saturate first, tasks spill over to Cloud, and remaining tasks are rejected gracefully.
Experiment_2_Overload_Scenario.actual: 13 tasks admitted (68.42%), 6 rejected due to insufficient capacity.

Experiment_3_Unauthorized_Access.setup: Tenant 'tenant_traffic' logged in and attempted to query tasks belonging to 'tenant_health'.
Experiment_3_Unauthorized_Access.expected: Security gateway denies request with 403 Forbidden and logs security audit trail.
Experiment_3_Unauthorized_Access.actual: Access blocked successfully: True. Error: 'SECURITY VIOLATION [403 Forbidden]: Tenant 'tenant_traffic' is denied access to private records of Tenant 'tenant_health'.'.

Experiment_4_Sensitivity_Tuning.setup: Edge node upgraded from 4 CPU / 8GB / 10ms to 8 CPU / 16GB / 5ms.
Experiment_4_Sensitivity_Tuning.expected: Upgraded Edge accommodates more latency-critical tasks, dropping cluster-wide average latency.
Experiment_4_Sensitivity_Tuning.actual: Average latency dropped from 80.0 ms to 75.42 ms; Edge VM count increased from 3 to 4.
